negative_findings.description: No public vendor announcement of an AML/KYC transaction-monitoring implementation at a Slovenian bank was found in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: English query on AML transaction monitoring go-lives in Slovenia returned only generic vendor listicles (SymphonyAI, ComplyAdvantage, Sumsub, Zigram) and the Banka Slovenije AML/CFT supervision page; the Slovenian-language query returned only generic AML explainers, a public-procurement IT guideline PDF and unrelated register pages. No named SI bank + named AML vendor pairing surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML/KYC is the single most deadline-dense regulatory area for SI banks (6th-round FATF/MONEYVAL evaluation ongoing 2025, AMLA/AML Package), yet the supplier channel appears publicly silent - meaning this workstream needs a different tactic (job ads, RFP leaks, conference speaker lists, bank annual reports) rather than vendor newsrooms.

negative_findings.description: Slovenian-language searching for vendor reference/customer pages ('reference', 'stranka', 'uvedba') is heavily polluted by unrelated senses of the words.
negative_findings.result_summary: 'referenca' in Slovenian overwhelmingly returns payment-reference (SI00/SI12 payment-order reference number) content; 'stranka' returns both 'customer' and 'political party'; 'dobavitelj' pulls generic supply-chain and procurement content. This crowded out vendor case-study pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future runs must use narrower local phrasing ('študija primera', 'uspešna zgodba', 'implementacija v banki', 'projekt za banko', site: restricted to vendor domains) or the local-language channel will keep under-delivering on this cell.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated public directory of IT/regtech suppliers to Slovenian banks was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a Slovenian supplier list/register serving NLB, NKBM, SKB, Addiko, Gorenjska banka etc. returned only bank-comparison consumer articles, forum threads and company-register pages - no association-maintained or media-maintained vendor directory.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The vendor map must be assembled bottom-up from individual vendor sites, conference sponsor lists and company registers; no shortcut exists, which raises the cost and the miss-rate of this cell.

negative_findings.description: The routine playbook path given in the brief could not be read from this machine.
negative_findings.result_summary: The stated path is a Windows Dropbox path (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/...), while this session runs on macOS; no equivalent local copy was located under the working directory.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This slice follows the inline METHOD in the brief only; any playbook-specific taxonomy or scoring conventions may not be exactly matched.

coverage_gaps.description: Only NLB and Bankart are well covered on the supplier side. NKBM/OTP banka, SKB (OTP), Addiko Bank, Gorenjska banka (AIK), Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica and Deželna banka Slovenije have no vendor-announcement trail collected yet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run per-bank vendor searches in sl and en for each of these institutions (bank name + 'implementacija' / 'rešitev' / 'partner' / 'go-live'), and check their group parents' (OTP, Intesa, Erste/Steiermärkische, AIK) group-level vendor announcements which often cover SI subsidiaries.

coverage_gaps.description: Regtech proper - regulatory reporting (AnaCredit, COREP/FINREP, ESG/CSRD reporting), sanctions screening, fraud/PSD3, and instant-payments VoP (Verification of Payee, October 2025 deadline) - has no confirmed SI vendor source yet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vendor newsrooms of BearingPoint (ABACUS), Regnology, Wolters Kluwer OneSumX, Vermeg, SAS, NICE Actimize, Featurespace, iBanFirst/VoP providers for Slovenia/SEE references; and check Bankart for VoP scheme implementation announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: Indirect reveal channels that are usually richer than press releases for private banks were not exploited: vendor job postings, bank job postings naming platforms, LinkedIn vendor case posts, GitHub/tech-blog traces, and bank annual reports' outsourcing/ICT third-party disclosures (now mandatory under DORA's register of information).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass over MojeDelo/Optius/LinkedIn job ads for platform names (Temenos, Vynamic, BASE24, Oracle FCCM, SAS AML) and over SI bank annual reports for outsourcing and ICT third-party sections.

coverage_gaps.description: None of the listed URLs were fetched or liveness-tested in this pass; several are section/index URLs constructed from observed article URLs rather than directly observed index pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass; for any 403/timeout treat as bot-defended-but-live and retry with a browser fetch, and for 404 re-derive the index URL from a known-good article URL.

brief: Slovenia's supplier-side trace is real but thin and highly concentrated: because the systemic banks are private, almost all public evidence of regulatory-driven IT projects flows through Bankart, the sector's shared card/payment processor, and through NLB. The richest confirmed sources are foreign vendor newsrooms announcing Bankart and NLB wins (Diebold Nixdorf/Vynamic replacing BASE24 in 2024, Nets instant payments in 2019, Iliad payment testing in 2025, Temenos core at NLB) plus a domestic layer of Slovenian-language suppliers - Halcom, SRC, SETCCE, Mikrografija, Payten/ASEE, Comtrade - whose compliance marketing dates obligations precisely. A second, underused channel is advisory and event material in Slovenian (PwC Slovenija DORA pages, Akademija Finance's ZInfV-1/DORA events, ZBS's Bančna konferenca, INFOSEK), where speaker and sponsor lists snowball the vendor map faster than press releases do. The main hole is AML/KYC and regulatory reporting: no public vendor-bank pairing surfaced in either language, so that sub-cell needs job ads, annual-report outsourcing disclosures and conference agendas rather than vendor newsrooms.
